title: High-Performance Data Processing & Polars (PYTH_152_S1 to PYTH_152_S8)

slides.title: Polars vs Pandas
slides.prompt: Polars is a lightning-fast DataFrame library written in Rust utilizing Apache Arrow for zero-copy memory operations.
slides.codeSnippet:
import polars as pl
df = pl.read_csv('large_dataset.csv')

slides.title: Lazy Evaluation
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to transform a standard Polars DataFrame into a LazyFrame for query optimization.

slides.title: Memory Optimization
slides.prompt: Why is Polars significantly faster and more memory-efficient than traditional Pandas 1.x?
options: It leverages Rust, Apache Arrow memory layout, and parallel query optimization
It converts all data into Python dictionaries
It forces all processing onto GPU only
slides.correctAnswer: It leverages Rust, Apache Arrow memory layout, and parallel query optimization

slides.title: Executing Lazy Queries
slides.prompt: Fill in the Polars method required to execute a LazyFrame pipeline and materialize the results.

slides.title: Column Expressions
slides.prompt: What is the recommended method to select and transform columns in Polars?
options: Iterating over rows using Python for-loops

slides.title: Creating New Columns
slides.prompt: Fill in the Polars method used to add or modify columns without dropping existing ones.

slides.title: Apache Arrow Format
slides.prompt: What primary advantage does Apache Arrow bring to data processing in Python?
options: Standardized columnar in-memory formatting for zero-copy data sharing between languages
Automatic conversion of databases to JSON
slides.correctAnswer: Standardized columnar in-memory formatting for zero-copy data sharing between languages
